questions: Can I study in Europe with low marks (below 60%)?
entries.answer: Yes — Hungary, Poland, Czech Republic, Malta, Cyprus, Romania and Slovakia are commonly explored for ~50–65% profiles when documents and funds are strong. Embassies decide visas; no ethical consultant guarantees approval.

questions: Can I study in Europe without IELTS?
entries.answer: Sometimes. Many universities accept medium-of-instruction (MOI) letters, internal English tests, or interviews — especially in Hungary, Poland, Czech Republic, Malta, Cyprus and some German programs. UK/Ireland/Australia usually need secure English tests.

questions: What is Germany Ausbildung and can international students apply?
entries.answer: Ausbildung is Germany’s dual vocational training: you train at a company and school while earning a monthly training salary (often roughly €900–€1,350). International applicants can apply with language (often A2–B1 German) and a training contract.

questions: Can I apply for Ausbildung without German language?
entries.answer: Rarely immediately. Most employers need A2–B1 (higher for nursing). Start language training while SK Immigration prepares CV, documents and employer matching.

questions: How much does it cost to study in Europe?
entries.answer: Budget destinations (Hungary, Poland, Romania) often total roughly USD 7,000–14,000/year including living. Germany may have low tuition but needs blocked-account planning (~€11k+ living proof). UK/Ireland/Netherlands/Australia cost more.

questions: How long does a student visa take?
entries.answer: Commonly 3–6 months from first consultation to departure: applications, offer, documents, and embassy processing. Germany Ausbildung and Canada/Australia can run longer if language or medical steps apply.

questions: Can I work while studying in Europe?
entries.answer: Usually yes with limits. Examples: Germany often 120 full or 240 half days/year; UK often 20 hrs/week in term; exact rules depend on your permit — always verify.

questions: What if my student visa is refused?
entries.answer: SK Immigration does not guarantee visas. After refusal we review the letter, fix document gaps, and advise reapplication or alternative countries. Embassy fees are usually non-refundable; service fees cover preparation, not outcomes.

questions: Can I apply for a student visa with a 3–5 year study gap?
entries.answer: Often yes if the Statement of Purpose explains the gap honestly (work, family, skills). Hungary, Poland and Czech Republic are frequently gap-friendlier. Gaps above 5 years need stronger justification.

questions: What documents are needed for a Schengen student visa?
entries.answer: Typically: passport, offer letter, proof of funds, insurance, accommodation, academic docs, SOP/CV, photos, form + fee. Country extras apply (Germany blocked account, Italy Dichiarazione di Valore, France Campus France).

questions: What is the difference between Apostille, MOFA and Musadaqa?
entries.answer: MOFA is foreign ministry attestation in your country. Apostille is Hague Convention legalization for member countries. Musadaqa refers to attestation chains used for Gulf (UAE etc.). SK Immigration handles attestation checklists end-to-end.

questions: What is a Germany blocked account (Sperrkonto)?
entries.answer: A blocked bank account proving you can fund living costs for a German study visa. Required amounts change — verify embassy guidance. Ausbildung applicants usually show salary via training contract instead.

questions: What is a CAS for UK student visa?
entries.answer: CAS means Confirmation of Acceptance for Studies issued by a licensed UK sponsor after you meet offer conditions (and usually pay a deposit). You need a CAS before applying for the Student visa on GOV.UK.

questions: What are Canada study permit requirements?
entries.answer: Letter of acceptance from a DLI, proof of funds, identity docs, and often biometrics/medical. Some intakes need a Provincial Attestation Letter (PAL). IRCC decides — SK Immigration prepares honest files.

questions: Which is the best country to study abroad on a low budget?
entries.answer: For many applicants: Malaysia, Turkey, Hungary, Poland, Romania, Slovakia and Cyprus offer lower total costs. Germany can be low-tuition but needs living-fund proof. “Best” depends on marks, language and career goal — take the free eligibility quiz.

questions: Hungary vs Poland for student visa — which is better?
entries.answer: Both are affordable EU options popular for flexible admissions. Compare program quality, city living costs, language, and your career target. Use SK’s country compare tool and free consultation.

questions: Germany vs UK for international students?
entries.answer: Germany: low public tuition, blocked account, German helpful for Ausbildung/jobs. UK: higher tuition, CAS + SELT, Graduate Route. Choose by budget, language and post-study plan.

questions: How does document attestation work for Dubai / UAE?
entries.answer: Degrees often need home-country attestation (HEC/MOFA etc.) then UAE embassy/consulate and UAE MOFA or approved channels (Musadaqa/QVP as applicable). SK Immigration provides attestation checklists and processing support.

questions: What are Schengen visit visa requirements?
entries.answer: Passport, form, photos, travel insurance (€30,000+ typical), itinerary, funds, employment/ties, and invitation if visiting family/friends. Refusal risk rises with weak home ties — prepare honestly.

entries.answer: Keep it clear, Europass-style, with photo if appropriate, language levels (A1–B2), education, and practical skills. Use SK’s free CV builder, then apply via the Ausbildung jobs board.

entries.answer: Because embassies and consulates make final decisions. Ethical consultancies prepare strong files and honest advice. Anyone promising “100% visa” is a red flag.

questions: What is an MOI letter for study abroad?
entries.answer: A Medium of Instruction letter from your school/college stating you studied in English. Some European universities accept MOI instead of IELTS. Not accepted everywhere (UK/Australia often need SELT).

questions: How much proof of funds do I need for a student visa?
entries.answer: It depends on the country: Germany uses blocked-account guidance; UK uses GOV.UK maintenance amounts; Canada uses IRCC funds tables; others need bank statements covering tuition + living. SK Immigration builds a country-specific funds plan.

questions: Best countries to study without IELTS in 2026?
entries.answer: Frequently explored: Hungary, Poland, Czech Republic, Malta, Cyprus, Romania, Malaysia, Turkey, and some German pathways. Always confirm the exact university’s 2026 intake rules.

questions: How to apply for Nursing Ausbildung in Germany?
entries.answer: Prepare German language (often B1+ for nursing), a clean CV, certificates, and apply to training providers. SK Immigration lists openings and guides documents — employers and embassies decide.

questions: Visit visa vs student visa — what’s the difference?
entries.answer: Visit visas are short stays for tourism/family/business and forbid study/work beyond narrow rules. Student visas allow full programs with residence permits. Never enter on a visit visa intending to study long-term — that risks refusal/bans.
